learning_outcomes.text: Students will have acquired comprehensive knowledge in Boolean algebra, the structure and function of basic digital circuits, cost optimization of digital functional groups, techniques for clock-synchronous data processing, data encoding and processing, and the structure and function of basic functionalities that are central components, especially in microprocessor architectures.
Students are able to understand basic circuit concepts of digital logic and functional blocks, analyze their interaction, evaluate their functionality, and develop simple blocks themselves.
The evaluation and development of multi-stage combinatorial logic blocks and Finite State Machines (FSMs) will be covered.
Students will learn the hardware description language Verilog, and Verilog examples will be given for each topic of the lecture. The lecture deals exclusively with (clock-) synchronous circuits.

assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam. The grade contributes 5/138 to the final grade.
